1. SINGLE-SCAN CONDITIONAL AGGREGATION — TARGET: the 15 repeated scalar subqueries over store_sales filtered by the five ss_quantity buckets (1–20, 21–40, 41–60, 61–80, 81–100) — TRANSFORMATION: Replace all count and avg subqueries with one scan of store_sales that computes, for every bucket, COUNT(*), AVG(ss_ext_tax), and AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) using conditional aggregate filters, then have the outer CASE expressions consume those precomputed bucket values.

2. RANGE PREDICATE PUSHDOWN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_quantity — TRANSFORMATION: Restrict the single store_sales scan to rows with ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 100, i.e. exactly the union of the five required buckets, so rows outside all buckets are never scanned or aggregated.

3. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: store_sales(ss_quantity) INCLUDE (ss_ext_tax, ss_net_paid_inc_tax) — TRANSFORMATION: If the single aggregated scan is still expensive, create a covering index on ss_quantity that also carries ss_ext_tax and ss_net_paid_inc_tax, allowing an index-only scan to answer all bucket counts and averages without touching the 57.6M-row heap.

4. PARALLEL AGGREGATION — TARGET: the rewritten single aggregate over store_sales — TRANSFORMATION: Make sure the consolidated aggregation can use PostgreSQL’s parallel seq/index scan and parallel aggregation, which the 10–15 independent scalar subqueries cannot use effectively.
